fresh_terms.name: ~k
fresh_terms.purpose: fresh symmetric session key generated by client C

long_term_keys.name: ltkS
long_term_keys.policy: private setup/state for server S; public key pk(ltkS), referred to as pkS in the input, is public and bound to S; reveal only via explicit Reveal(...) if modeled

messages.label: M1
messages.meaning: Client C sends its freshly generated symmetric key ~k encrypted under server S's public key pkS.

messages.label: M2
messages.meaning: Server S confirms receipt of the key by hashing the plaintext key k_M1 decrypted from M1 and sending the hash back to C.

checks.condition: using ltkS, decrypt M1 as aenc(k_M1, pk(ltkS)) and bind plaintext k_M1; no tag, sender identity, or freshness check is described
received M2 must be syntactically equal to h(~k), where ~k is the fresh key retained from C_send_M1

events.name: SessionKeyGenerated
events.when: C generates the fresh symmetric key ~k for S and sends M1

events.name: ServerConfirm
events.when: S has decrypted M1 with ltkS and sends h(k_M1) as M2

events.name: Commit
events.when: C receives a message equal to h(~k) and accepts the server confirmation

events.name: Secret
events.when: C completes after verifying the hash confirmation for ~k

claims.intent: For every accepted client session, the client-generated session key ~k should not become known to the Dolev-Yao adversary, absent any explicit reveal or compromise behavior.
claims.witness: universal all-traces secrecy goal; no finite witness supplied

claims.intent: If C accepts the hash confirmation for ~k as coming from S, then S must previously have decrypted a ciphertext under S's private key and sent a confirmation for the same key.
claims.witness: universal all-traces authentication goal; no finite witness supplied

claims.intent: Injective client authentication for accepted client sessions over the fresh key ~k: distinct client Commit events for the same authenticated session data should not be justified by the same protocol instance; exact formula not supplied in the NL input.
claims.witness: universal all-traces injective-authentication goal; no finite witness supplied

claims.intent: There exists an honest execution in which C generates a fresh key, S receives/decrypts it, S returns its hash, and C accepts.
claims.witness: C_send_M1; S_recv_M1_send_M2 with k_M1 = ~k; C_recv_M2_accept after checking M2 = h(~k)

compromise.policy: No reveal, key-compromise, corruption, or long-term-key exposure behavior is mentioned in the protocol input or supplied goals. Do not add reveal exceptions unless an explicit Reveal(...) behavior is added by a later modeling contract.

abstractions: The public key name pkS from the prose is normalized to the symbolic term pk(ltkS), with pkS recorded as an alias.
The symmetric key k is modeled as a fresh atom ~k used as a session key; no symmetric-encryption operation is described.
No tags, identities, or session identifiers are added to either message, because the prose says only the key is encrypted and only the hash of the key is returned.
The from/to fields record intended protocol roles; in the Dolev-Yao network they are not authenticated transport metadata.
The server-side key variable k_M1 denotes the plaintext obtained by decrypting M1; in an honest run k_M1 = ~k.
modeling_assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.
The public key pk(ltkS) is available to C and the adversary and is bound to server S at setup.
C retains ~k and intended peer S between sending M1 and checking M2.
S responds to any decryptable M1 under pk(ltkS); the prose does not describe checking that the plaintext was generated by C.
C accepts only if the received second message equals h(~k).
resolved_open_questions: No reference Sapic+ or Tamarin code is embedded in the input, so this IR uses only the natural-language description and user-supplied goal metadata.
No compromise behavior is described; the IR records no reveal events.
The prose does not describe message tags or identities; the IR intentionally omits them instead of strengthening the protocol.
The prose's pkS notation is resolved as pk(ltkS) with pkS as an alias.

semantic_constraints.policy: Message order is M1 from C to S followed by M2 from S to C in an honest execution.
M1 plaintext consists only of ~k; no tag, C identity, S identity, or transcript data is included.
M2 consists only of h(k_M1); no tag, C identity, S identity, or ciphertext reference is included.
ServerConfirm(S,k_M1) may be emitted only after S has decrypted M1 with ltkS and before or while S sends h(k_M1).
Commit(C,S,~k) and Secret(C,S,~k) may be emitted only by C after receiving a term equal to h(~k).
No server event asserts knowledge of C's identity, because M1 contains no client identity and the network sender field is adversary-controlled under Dolev-Yao semantics.
Replay of M1 or M2 is part of the adversarial network behavior and is not prevented by tags or nonces beyond the freshness of ~k.
